<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The walk animation logic is now clear.

A potential bug was found in `runPredictionAnimation`. When the forward pass reaches the leaf node, the function switches to backward mode without decrementing the path index. This means the first backward tick will start at the leaf instead of moving upward. The backward pass logic needs closer inspection.

The backward pass creates a jump effect rather than a smooth continuous animation. Each tick decrements the path index, so the particle animates across the next edge upward instead of following the previous step. The highlight remains on the leaf during the first backward frame while the particle moves toward the parent.

The backward pass logic is actually correct. The particle animates from the leaf up to the parent on the first backward tick. After reaching the root, the particle check `pathIndex < 1` suppresses animation because the root is index zero. This means the final edge is handled properly and no extra tick is needed.

Finishing the last tree resets the path index to the leaf. This jump back to the leaf may be intentional but appears visually odd.

The particle key uses `${from}-${to}-${flow}`. Because the flow changes without altering the from and to coordinates, React treats the particle as unchanged during the backward transition.

During the backward pass, the highlighted path shrinks from the leaf end as the index decreases. This suggests the leaf loses its highlight while returning, which may be intentional or a bug.

For single-node trees, the animation skips all forward particles because the path length is one. It immediately switches to backward mode on the first interval tick.

A major race condition was discovered in the `focusTree` effect. When `focusTree` changes during the walk animation, the effect's cleanup function calls `clearTimer`, which stops the walk animation prematurely.

The stage effect at lines 79-88 does not depend on `focusTree`, so it avoids the premature timer clear. The shrinking highlight during the upward pass is likely a UX bug.

The SVG motion animations use `fill="freeze"` and `repeatCount="1"`. Because the interval ticks every 480 milliseconds while each animation lasts 550 milliseconds, the transitions may overlap or cut off.

A potential edge case exists where `pathIndex` could drop to zero before the backward flow begins, causing the particle condition `pathIndex < 1` to suppress the first backward particle entirely.
</details></think>
